facts.value: The transistor is properly biased to operate in the active region for amplification of signals. The common-emitter (CE) configuration is used, where the base terminal is the input line, the emitter terminal is the common-ground for input and output, and the collector terminal is the output line.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electronic and Computer Engineering

facts.value: A weak signal that we want to amplify is applied to the base terminal of the transistor amplifier circuit.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electronic and Computer Engineering

facts.value: A small current flowing into the base of the transistor can cause a large current to flow out from the collector which is proportional to the base current, but much larger than that.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor/Master of Engineering in Electronic and Computer Engineering

facts.value: The resulting amplified output signals are received at the collector terminal, which is the amplified version of the input signal.
